items.body:
## Summary

`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` is the block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter published for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. On current `main` the pair cannot be served: `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2",...}'` fails during startup, and fixing one failure exposes the next. This PR makes the combination start and serve on NVIDIA (8x H100, TP8 + EP), adds unit coverage for the two non-model changes, and reports a throughput sweep against the existing MTP path. No kernels, defaults, or MTP behaviour are changed.

The three blockers on `main` (9d4d9aa5bc), in the order they surface:

| # | Stage | Error on `main` | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | draft model load | `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface` | `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (the architecture the DFlash2 checkpoint targets) do not declare `SupportsEagle3`, and `Glm5NextModel` is not an `EagleModelMixin`, so the DFlash speculator cannot register its aux hidden-state layers (`target_layer_ids + 1 = [6, 15, 25, 34, 43]`). |
| 2 | KV cache init | `NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.` | `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` bails out as soon as a non-MLA attention layer (the draft's sliding-window GQA layers) is present, so the generic page unifier runs on a spec set it cannot unify (MLA 655,360 B, indexer 21,120 B and draft 163,840 B pages at block_size 640). |
| 3 | config | `ValueError: Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled` | `create_draft_parallel_config` copies `enable_expert_parallel` from the MoE target onto the dense drafter (introduced by #55914 for the DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE drafter). |

### Changes

- **`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py` (aux hidden-state capture).** `Glm5NextModel` becomes an `EagleModelMixin`; `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` declare `SupportsEagle3`. The tensor handed to the drafter is not `hidden_states + residual`: GLM-5.3-Flash layers run mHC with 4 residual streams and defer each layer's `hc_post` into the next layer's fused post+pre kernel, so at a layer boundary `residual` is the widened `(T, 4 * hidden)` stream (a naive `hidden + residual` fails with `The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1`) and `hidden_states` alone is the raw layer output. `_aux_hidden_state()` completes the deferred `hc_post` through a dedicated `MHCPostOp` and contracts the streams back to `hidden_size` with `hc_contract`, which is the quantity SGLang's `_prepare_aux_hidden_state` feeds DFlash2. The capture is read-only: the layer loop keeps consuming the original `(hidden_states, residual, post, comb)` tuple. Non-mHC layer boundaries already carry the summed stream in `hidden_states` and are returned as-is. When any aux layer is requested, `forward` returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)`; otherwise the return type is unchanged.

### Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate check run on 2026-09-15)

Searches: `gh pr list --state open --search "dflash glm"`, `"GLM-5.3 speculative draft"`, `"create_draft_parallel_config"`, `"enable_expert_parallel draft model"`, `gh pr list --state all --search "dflash"`, `gh issue list --search "GLM-5.3-Flash dflash"`.

- #55682 (Leoyzen, open) implements the aux capture with the same semantics (materialize `hc_post`, then `hc_contract`, at the layer boundary) and adds a CPU unit suite for it. It intentionally leaves the KV-cache layout to a companion change (its description notes the draft sliding-window groups still need one); on the configuration tested here (TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, H100) `main` + an aux-capture-only change still fails at blocker 2. The `model.py` change here is functionally equivalent for GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC boundaries; if #55682 lands first, this PR rebases onto it and drops its `model.py` hunk.
- #55423 (zixi-qi, draft, needs-rebase) covers aux capture plus a KV layout, but with a different layout design: the draft's sliding-window layers are re-blocked to the MLA block size, padded to the MLA page and aliased into the target's MLA slots (no extra bytes per block; `is_eagle_group` follows `use_eagle_block_drop()`; tested with `disable_eagle_block_drop=true`). This PR keeps the draft in a separate region with its native page instead; it is simpler and needs no block-drop override, but it costs KV capacity (numbers below). The two are alternative designs for reviewers to choose between.
- #56933 (hnt2601, opened 2026-09-15) is the same EP-inheritance fix with a different signature (`draft_model_config: ModelConfig | None`). If it merges first, this PR drops the `speculative.py` hunk.
- #55219 (ivanium, draft) removes the GLM-specific layout in favour of the generic packed layout; if that lands, the `kv_cache_utils.py` part of this PR is superseded.
- #54451 (ROCm: glm5next lacks `SupportsEagle3`) is the ROCm counterpart of blocker 1; this PR only touches the NVIDIA model file.

No open PR makes `GLM-5.3-Flash + GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` start on `main` end to end; this one does, and the parts overlapping with #55682 and #56933 are flagged above for rebasing.

Due to discussion for kv cache allocation,  this PR just submits the main support in advance.

## Previous full supported performance

**Setup.** 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 535.154.05), TP8 + EP, torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Python 3.12, vLLM `main` 9d4d9aa5bc + this branch, V2 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Target `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-model-len 131072`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). Draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window layers, sliding window 2048, block_size 8). Auto-selected attention backends: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (target), FLASH_ATTN (draft).

**Workload.** 16 fixed prompts (code and prose), greedy (`temperature=0`), `max_tokens=512`, `/v1/chat/completions`. Single stream = 4 sequential prompts after 2 warm-ups; concurrency N = N simultaneous requests (prompts cycled). Aggregate output tok/s, per-request median tok/s in parentheses. `k` = `num_speculative_tokens`, "FA" / "FI" = FlashAttention / FlashInfer draft attention, the number in the config column is `--max-num-seqs`.

| Config | Single stream | Conc 8 | Conc 32 | Conc 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16, FA, 48 | 178.7 | 848.5 (118.3) | 707.3 (23.1) | - |
| DFlash2 k=8, FA, 48 | 202.1 | 987.7 (136.3) | 2652.5 (94.5) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FA, 48 | 218.5 | 1064.5 (145.2) | 2844.3 (101.2) | - |
| DFlash2 k=4, FA, 48 | 220.3 | 1051.3 (148.0) | 2751.6 (98.8) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FI, 48 | 202.1 | 1021.0 (141.1) | 2578.8 (95.1) | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 1) | **223.0** | **1074.0 (145.2)** | **2850.7 (103.9)** | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 2) | **225.5** | - | **2923.6 (106.7)** | **4269.3 (77.5)** |
| MTP k=5, 96 (baseline) | 160.7 | 853.7 (117.3) | 2377.0 (84.0) | 3721.3 (66.7) |

Acceptance, aggregated from every `SpecDecoding metrics` log line of each run:

| Config | Mean acceptance length | Draft acceptance rate | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16 | 3.63 | 16.5% | 0.75, 0.54, 0.39, 0.28, 0.20, 0.14, 0.10, 0.08, 0.05, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.006, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001 |
| DFlash2 k=8 | 3.33 | 29.1% | 0.75, 0.53, 0.36, 0.25, 0.18, 0.12, 0.08, 0.06 |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 3.31 | 38.5% | 0.77, 0.55, 0.39, 0.28, 0.19, 0.13 |
| DFlash2 k=4 | 3.00 | 49.9% | 0.78, 0.56, 0.39, 0.27 |
| MTP k=5 | 3.13 | 42.7% | 0.81, 0.57, 0.37, 0.23, 0.15 |

Takeaways:

- `num_speculative_tokens` is the dominant knob. Acceptance decays to ~0 beyond position 8 (the drafter's block_size), so k=16 pays a 17-token verify per step for the same ~3.3-3.6 accepted tokens; going to k=6 raises conc-32 throughput from 707 to 2924 tok/s (4.1x). k=4..6 is the sweet spot on this workload, k=8 is slightly worse.
- Against MTP k=5 at identical settings, DFlash2 k=6 is faster at every concurrency: +40% single stream, +26% at 8, +23% at 32, +15% at 64.
- FlashInfer as the draft attention backend is 7-9% slower than the auto-selected FlashAttention.
- `--max-num-seqs 96` vs 48: +2-3%, no preemption at concurrency 64.

**KV cache capacity (cost of the separate draft region).**

| Config | Available KV memory | KV capacity | Max concurrency at 131072 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP k=5 | 23.61 GiB | 1,802,673 tokens | 13.75x |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 23.49 GiB | 1,358,649 tokens | 10.37x |

Per block (block_size 640) the target uses 11 x 655,360 B MLA pages plus 11 x 21,120 B indexer pages (kpool tails aliased into them); the draft adds 5 x 163,840 B pages and its own per-request block demand to the group-aware capacity estimate, hence 24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory. #55423's slot-aliasing design avoids this at the price of re-blocking the draft to the MLA page; that is the main trade-off between the two PRs. At `--max-num-seqs 96` this still leaves ~14k tokens per sequence.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group "tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters" -v

# Lint and types
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py

# Serve (8x H100)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-num-seqs 96 --max-model-len 131072 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":6}'
# MTP baseline: same command with --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

# Tool-calling E2E: 8 scenarios against /v1/chat/completions (auto / required / named tool_choice, zero-arg tool, no tools, thinking off, streaming, multi-turn), see Test Result
# Throughput sweep: 16 prompts, greedy, max_tokens=512, single stream + concurrency {8,32} / {32,64}; per-config server relaunch with the speculative-config JSON above
# Accuracy
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** `3 passed` (the kv-cache test and both parametrizations of the config test).

**pre-commit.** All hooks pass on the five changed files, including `mypy-3.10` (the follow-up commit fixes a `dict` invariance error in `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next`).

**Startup.** Each blocker above was hit and cleared in turn on this branch; the final configuration loads the draft (5 layers, `Overriding draft model max model len from 1048576 to 131072`), builds the KV cache (`GPU KV cache size: 1,358,649 tokens`), captures CUDA graphs and serves.

**Tool-calling E2E** against the running DFlash2 server (`--tool-call-parser glm47`, `--reasoning-parser glm45`): 8/8 pass, zero FSM or CUDA errors in the server log. Repeated after each sweep configuration with the same result.

| Scenario | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| auto tool call | `tool_choice=auto`, one `<tool_call>` parsed into `tool_calls`, arguments valid JSON | PASS |
| required tool call | `tool_choice=required` forces a call | PASS |
| named tool call | `tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}` picks the named tool | PASS |
| named zero-argument tool | tool without parameters yields `arguments == "{}"` | PASS |
| no tools, plain chat | no tool schema, ordinary completion, no stray tags | PASS |
| thinking off | `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` with tools | PASS |
| streaming tool call | `stream=true`, deltas reassemble to a valid call | PASS |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back, second assistant turn answers from it | PASS |

**GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, `--max-concurrency 1 --request-timeout-seconds 7200`; the default 600 s timeout acts as a global deadline at concurrency 1 and truncates the run).**

| Server | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target only (no speculative config), same machine and flags | 0.931 | 0.0% | 121,390 | 1195 s | 101.6 |
| DFlash2 k=6 (this PR) | 0.939 | 0.0% | 123,732 | 607 s | 203.8 |

The two accuracies differ by 0.8 points (about 10 of 1319 questions), inside the run-to-run spread of this greedy-but-nondeterministic stack (see below); output-token counts match within 2%. DFlash2 delivers the same accuracy at 2.0x the single-stream decode speed.

**Greedy output determinism.** Exact token-level lossless verification is not possible on this stack: with `temperature=0` the same server produces different continuations run to run (16 sweep prompts, 512 tokens, sequential, prompt already cached): target-only 0/16 identical across three runs (median common prefix 272-306 characters before the first divergence), DFlash2 k=6 0/16 identical across three runs (median 237-306), and DFlash2 vs target-only 0/16 identical (median 222-237). The run-to-run spread of the target alone is the same size as the DFlash2-vs-target spread, so the divergence comes from the fp8 MoE + EP numerics of the target (near-tie argmax flips), not from the speculative path; the GSM8K parity above (0.919 vs 0.911) is the meaningful losslessness check.

**Pre-existing crash observed while testing, not introduced by this PR (#55626).** Any step that co-schedules a ~600+ token prefill with a speculative verify step, or a burst of a dozen ~630-token prefills, kills the engine with an asynchronous CUDA fault. It reproduces identically with MTP, whose KV layout on this branch is byte-for-byte the `main` layout, so it is a property of the target's FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA path with speculative decoding, matching the traceback location and the FlashInfer core dump posted in #55626.

| Run | Speculative config | Load | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | DFlash2 k=6 | `gsm8k_eval.py` unbounded (100 in flight): 12 prefills of 618-645 tokens in one step, 7578 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, all 8 workers, reproduced 3/3 |
| A' | DFlash2 k=6, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | same | fault attributed to FlashInfer `BatchMLAPagedAttentionSM90` in the target's `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py::forward_mqa` (`Failed to run MLA, error: an illegal memory access was encountered`) |
| B | DFlash2 k=6 | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 661-token prefill + one 7-token verify step | `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` (sticky error surfacing in the next GEMM) |
| C | MTP k=5 (main layout) | unbounded: 7 prefills, 4518 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` |
| D | MTP k=5 (main layout) | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 637-token prefill + one 6-token verify step | `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered`, surfacing at `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py:350 _kv_lens_host` (the same frame as in #55626) |

The throughput sweep and the tool-calling E2E never hit it because their concurrent prompts are short (~30 tokens) and their long prompts run one at a time; GSM8K was therefore run at `--max-concurrency 1`. Prefix caching is not involved (`prefix_cache_stats ... hits=0` in every crash dump).

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- #55626 (above) affects every speculative configuration of GLM-5.3-Flash on SM90 and needs a separate fix; the DFlash2 path inherits it.
- The separate draft region costs KV capacity relative to the slot-aliasing design in #55423 (24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory); the two designs should be reconciled in review.
- Aux hidden states are not all-gathered under sequence parallelism (`compilation_config.pass_config.enable_sp`); the tested configuration runs with compilation mode NONE, where SP is off. Pipeline parallelism is already gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash and was not exercised.
- Tested with greedy sampling for throughput and the default sampling of the tool-calling scripts; `disable_eagle_block_drop` was left at its default.
- Only the NVIDIA model file is changed; the ROCm copy (#54451) is not addressed.

items.title: Enable support for Terratorch models in v2 engine
items.body:
## Purpose

Terratorch models (Prithvi, TerraMind, etc.) were already supported in vLLM via the
existing `Terratorch` model class. This PR extends that support to the **V2 engine**
by fixing three issues that prevent Terratorch pooling models from loading or running
under the V2 model runner.

- **`terratorch.py`** — `SupportsMultiModal.get_language_model()` walks child modules
  looking for a `VllmModel` instance. `Terratorch` is a pure pooling model with no
  inner language model, so the default implementation always raises
  `NotImplementedError`. Adding `get_language_model(self): return self` satisfies the
  interface contract and removes the need for a workaround subclass in the terratorch
  package.

- **`pooling_runner.py`** — The V2 pooling runner validates the selected task against
  an explicit allowlist. Terratorch models register task type `"plugin"` to signal that
  output post-processing is fully owned by the model plugin. This type was absent from
  the allowlist, causing the V2 engine to reject the model at startup.

- **`rejection_sampler.py`** — `get_max_chunk_logits` divides by `vocab_size`. During
  V2 warm-up this is called for all models including pooling models. Terratorch has no
  text vocabulary (`vocab_size == 0`), triggering a `ZeroDivisionError` even though
  speculative decoding is never used for pooling models. An early-return guard when
  `vocab_size == 0` prevents the crash.

## Test Plan

Run Terratorch inference (Prithvi / TerraMind) with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` and
verify the model loads, warms up, and produces correct embeddings end-to-end.

## Test Result

Terratorch models load and run correctly under the V2 engine. All three failure modes
(startup rejection, `NotImplementedError`, `ZeroDivisionError`) are resolved.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.

- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

items.title: [Model] Fix K2-Horizon MoVA weight loading and support GPTQ INT4
items.body:
## Purpose
Fix K2-Horizon MoVA value-expert weight loading for quantized (GPTQ) checkpoints and tensor parallelism, and serve symmetric GPTQ INT4 MoVA value experts on both CUDA and XPU.

## Problem & Background
1. **GPTQ could not load at all**: upstream K2-Horizon defines `v_experts` as a list of `ColumnParallelLinear`, and `compute_mova_v_sparse` stacks a plain `.weight`:
   ```python
   w1 = torch.stack([expert.weight for expert in self.v_experts], dim=0).contiguous()
   ```
   AutoGPTQ checkpoints only have `qweight`, `scales` and `qzeros`, so this fails with `AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'`. The workaround was to keep MoVA out of quantization (`--fp_layers "v_experts,v_router"`), which leaves ~14 GiB of value experts in BF16.
2. **TP sharding broken**: `load_weights` used a hand-rolled `chunk(dim=0)` for `v_experts`. Quantized weights have the output dimension on axis 1, so TP > 1 fails shape assertions.
3. **CUDA not covered** (raised in jsboige/vllm#50): the first revision of this PR read `qweight` after the XPU linear kernel's post-load transpose, so it was gated to `XPUwNa16LinearKernel` and raised `NotImplementedError` on CUDA, where AutoGPTQ repacks for Marlin.

## Solution
1. **Fused value experts**: replace the `ColumnParallelLinear` list with one `MergedColumnParallelLinear` (`v_experts_fused`), with `shard_id = expert_id`, following `qk_proj` / `gate_up_proj`. vLLM's standard weight loader then handles TP sharding for unquantized and quantized weights.
2. **Platform-independent INT4 layout**: `K2HorizonMoVAWNA16Method` replaces the linear method on `v_experts_fused`. After loading, it transposes the raw GPTQ `qweight` / `scales` into the fused-MoE `int4_w4a16` layout (`[E, N, K // 2]` uint8, low nibble = even k; `[E, N, K // group]` scales). The Triton kernel and the CUDA `moe_wna16` kernel both read this layout. Marlin / XPU linear repacking is skipped. On XPU these are the same bytes the previous revision got from the XPU kernel.
3. **Custom op**: MoVA value experts run through `vllm::k2_horizon_mova_experts`. items.body:
## Purpose

Add support for custom logits processors to Model Runner V2, mirroring the V1 feature with V2's batch model (#47172).

- a new `LogitsProcessor` ABC under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logits_processor/` with a single `add_request()` lifecycle keyed by the persistent slot index — no BatchUpdate ledger and no removal hook (V2 slots are never moved and freed slots are never indexed, so add-side overwrite is sufficient)
- `LogitsProcRequestState`, a narrow frozen struct passed to `__init__` that exposes only the fields a processor may read (token history, device, max_num_reqs, vocab_size), so `RequestState` stays out of the interface
- `LogitsContext`, the per-step batch layout passed to `apply()` — V2 reorders and expands logits rows every step, so a row is not a request
- a V2-own loader that validates entrypoint plugins and FQCNs against the V2 interface at load time, rejecting V1-interface processors with a clear error instead of crashing mid-sampling
- adoption of the interface by the built-in sampler states (logit bias, penalties, bad words): `add_request() -> bool` is OR-ed into `needs_logits_processing`, and `apply_staged_writes()` is the optional per-step flush hook for host-staged writes
- removes "custom logits processors" from the V2-unsupported gate: they no longer force a silent fallback to the V1 runner (or a hard error when V2 is forced)
- ports V1's `validate_params` to the V2 interface as an optional classmethod, dispatched at request admission by the active model runner: V1 keeps the existing path byte for byte, V2 runs the new entry

No behavior change for the pre-existing sampling stages; their pipeline order is unchanged. Custom processors run after the built-in stages and before thinking-budget forcing and temperature.

Documents the MRV2 logits processor interface in `docs/features/custom_logitsprocs.md`.

## Duplicate work check

#47585 adapts the V1 interface via a bridge: it diffs the row→request assignment every step to synthesize V1 `BatchUpdate` events, and mirrors output tokens on CPU from the AsyncOutput D2H copy. That doesn't fit MRV2:

1. **MRV2 has no BatchUpdate.** V1 needs the added/removed/moved ledger only because its batch indices compact and move; MRV2 slots are persistent and never moved. The bridge re-derives via per-step diffs what the runner already knows — a synthetic event stream instead of real lifecycle calls.
2. **The persistent batch model differs.** MRV2 reorders logits rows every step and expands them under speculative decoding (a row is not a request). The bridge assumes V1's row==request semantics, pays a per-step CPU diff + D2H sync to reconstruct state MRV2 already keeps on-device, and cannot represent draft rows — so it inherits V1's "no custom processors under spec decode" restriction, which MRV2-native processors don't have.
3. The bridge keeps V1's runtime costs (per-step diffing, CPU token mirrors, argmax-invariance routing) instead of exploiting MRV2's strengths (stable slots, on-device token history, admission gating via `add_request()`'s return).

This PR therefore implements a V2-native interface and rejects V1-interface processors at load time with a clear error, rather than wrapping them.

## Test Plan

- New CPU-only loader tests (`tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py`): V1-interface rejection via class object / FQCN / entrypoint, non-type and unimportable FQCNs, pooling-model rejection, load order, `validate_params` admission behavior.
- New GPU integration test (`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py`): a recording custom processor driven through `Sampler` — hook order, logits modification, pipeline position (post-bias, pre-temperature).
- New regressions: custom processor's `add_request()` return gating `needs_logits_processing`; slot reuse clearing bad-words state; custom LPs absent from the V2-unsupported gate (`tests/test_config.py`); `verify()` stays runner-agnostic (`tests/test_sampling_params.py`).
- Adapted existing suites: logit bias, bad words, sampler flags, thinking budget.
- E2E on NVIDIA GB200 with Qwen/Qwen3-8B: `vllm serve` with a target-token custom processor (correctness: forced output matches the target token exactly; untouched requests unaffected), `vllm bench serve` baseline vs loaded-processor throughput, and startup rejection of a V1-interface processor.

```

    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logit_bias.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_bad_words.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py \
    tests/test_config.py::test_v2_model_runner_supports_custom_logits_processors \
    tests/test_sampling_params.py::test_verify_leaves_logits_processors_to_admission -v
```

## Purpose
  Kimi-K3's shared MLA implementation (`nvidia/mla.py`) calls two CUDA-only fused custom ops on every prefill/decode step. Neither has an XPU registration, so Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B (and other Kimi-K3-family models) crash with `AttributeError: '_OpNamespace' '_C' object has no attribute
  '...'` on first attention forward on XPU.

  Adds a `vllm/models/kimi_k3/xpu/` package that re-exports the NVIDIA implementation's model/MTP classes rather than forking them: `nvidia/mla.py`'s fused-op call sites have no CUDA-specific Python branching, so they dispatch correctly on XPU tensors as soon as an XPU SYCL
  implementation of `fused_kimi_k3_mla_{key,decode}_concat_kv_cache_insert` is registered under the same op schema — see vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#592.

  Also widens two `is_cuda`-only asserts in `nvidia/kda_metadata.py` to accept any non-CPU device. These guard Triton launchers that are already platform-generic — their PDL branch is gated by `is_arch_support_pdl()`, `False` on XPU — so only the device check itself was CUDA-only.
  In-place fix rather than an XPU fork, since there's no vendor-specific alternative implementation to route to here.

  **Dependency:** requires the op registration from vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#592 to actually run; alone, this is a no-op on other platforms and adds a code path on XPU that isn't exercised until that PR is installed alongside it.

  Related to vllm-project/vllm#56422 (tracking issue combining this PR and vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#592).

items.title: [Feat][Model] Support encoder-side SWA-bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps a 128-token sliding-window (SWA) KV cache per layer beside its prefix-cacheable compressed MLA and indexer caches. Storing that window for prefix caching and KV connectors costs more than it saves, so this implements DeepSeek's encoder-side "SWA bounded replay": the SWA caches leave prefix caching, and after a prefix hit ending at H the scheduler recomputes the hit's last window [H-128, H) to rebuild them. The replayed tokens keep their cached KV in every other group, their window attention reads nothing below H-128, and decode always sees a full window. Outputs after a hit are therefore not bit-identical to a cold run, by design.

- KV cache spec: `SlidingWindowMLASpec(bounded_replay=True)` derives `prefix_cacheable=False` and `prefix_replay_tokens=sliding_window`; `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` forwards both to the worker.
- Scheduler: a hit records `Request.replay_start = H-128` and rewinds the computed count by the window; async KV-connector loads replay once the KV arrives; chunks ending inside the replayed range allocate nothing new; hits no longer than the window are not adopted.
- Worker: only DeepSeek-V4.1 replays, so `DeepseekV41ModelState` owns the per-request replay start. `add_request` stores it; `prepare_attn` gathers it for the batch's prefills, pads the replayed tokens' slots in the prefix-cacheable groups with one Triton kernel, and hands the starts to the sparse SWA metadata builder through a `ModelSpecificAttnMetadata`. The runner core is untouched apart from an optional `model_specific_attn_metadata` argument on `DefaultModelState.prepare_attn`.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 kernels clamp the window at `replay_start`: the SWA index and gather-length kernels, the FlashInfer mixed index kernel and the FlashMLA combine kernel. The compressed slot mappings (MLA and indexer) inherit the padding of the tokens' own slots, so a replayed token never re-enters the compressed caches.
- Switch: `--swa-bounded-replay` (`CacheConfig.swa_bounded_replay`, default on), read by the V4.1 attention layer. Needs model runner V2 and no prefill context parallelism; otherwise it logs once and keeps the SWA cache in prefix caching.
- One bugfix rides along as its own commit: KV-connector hits are taken in whole blocks under replay.

Known gap: a running request restarted in place under `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute` keeps its worker-side replay boundary and would recompute with a stale clamp; a follow-up will preempt such requests instead. No other open PR implements SWA replay.

## Usage

Nothing to configure: DeepSeek-V4.1 replays by default on model runner V2. `--no-swa-bounded-replay` restores the previous behaviour (SWA KV stored in the prefix cache). With replay on, KV connectors transfer only the MLA and indexer caches, and hits of at most 128 tokens are not adopted.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

Accuracy: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on TP4 GB200 with `vllm serve`, gsm8k (5-shot) run twice against the same server; pass 2 re-sends every prompt, so each request is a full-prompt prefix hit that replays only its last window (92.6% prefix-cache hit rate).

## Test Result

All listed tests pass; pre-commit and mypy are clean.

| gsm8k, n=1319 (pass 1 cold / pass 2 all hits) | replay on (this PR) | replay off (`--no-swa-bounded-replay`) |
|---|---|---|
| exact_match (flexible-extract) | 0.9272 / 0.9212 | 0.9295 / 0.9295 |

Both arms are within run-to-run noise (one standard error at n=1319 is 0.0075); the gap is the same in pass 1, where only the shared few-shot prefix is replayed. An earlier two-pass GPQA-diamond run on an internal pre-release checkpoint showed the same parity (0.6869 / 0.6919 with replay vs 0.7020 / 0.6869 without, n=198).

items.title: [WIP][Model] Add upcoming XingChen4 model support
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for the upcoming **XingChen4** MoE causal model.

XingChen4 reuses the DeepSeek-V2/V3 backbone (MLA attention, MoE block, optional DSA indexer) and replaces the standard residual connection with **Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC)**: the residual stream is expanded into `num_residual_streams` parallel streams mixed by input-dependent, doubly-stochastic matrices produced via Sinkhorn-Knopp projection. The mHC math matches the shared ops in `vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc`, so no private kernels are introduced.
Additionally, this PR enables optional FlagOS/FlagGems acceleration for XingChen4: it enables the hot-path kernels (MoE, attention, softmax, topk, etc.) and brings measurable end-to-end inference speedups — up to 19.87% TTFT and 26.32% TPOT reduction on high-concurrency long-prompt workloads (H100 benchmark), opt-in and disabled by default.

> **Status: Draft.** Model weights are not yet public on Hugging Face Hub. This PR is opened for early code review. Once weights are released, I will:
> 1. add a test entry in `tests/models/registry.py`
> 2. update `docs/models/supported_models.md`
> 3. mark the PR ready for review.

## Changes

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/xingchen4.py`: full model implementation (`XingChen4ForCausalLM`), including forward pass, mHC adapter, and tensor-parallel `load_weights()`.
2. Register `XingChen4ForCausalLM` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` and related `__init__.py`.
3. Reasoning parser (`vllm/reasoning/xingchen4_reasoning_parser.py`) for reasoning-capable variants.
4. Tool parser (`vllm/tool_parsers/xingchen4_tool_parser.py`) for auto tool calling.
5. Register `xingchen4` in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`, and `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`.

## Optional FlagGems acceleration (opt-in)

An optional acceleration path is gated behind the env var `USE_FLAGOS=1` (disabled by default). When set, it enables a curated subset of FlagGems kernels via `flag_gems.only_enable(include=[...])`.

> **Scope note:** The acceleration is only enabled from the XingChen4 model path — the flag_gems.only_enable(...) call lives exclusively inside xingchen4.py and is gated behind the env var, so no other model load path triggers it. The whitelist is intentionally narrow (...), and with the env var unset the behavior is fully unchanged. 
 For completeness: only_enable substitutes operators at the PyTorch dispatch level, so once enabled the kernels apply to any op in the same process that matches the whitelist — we therefore consider this an acceleration prototype and welcome feedback on a more scoped kernel backend.

```bash
pip install flagtree==0.6.1 flag-gems==5.3.4 -i https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-nvidia/simple            # see version constraints in the PR discussion
USE_FLAGOS=1 vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xingchen4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xingchen4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

All XingChen4 hot-path tests below run with FlagGems **disabled**.

## Benchmark method (H100 × 1)

- Framework: this branch vs. vanilla vLLM baseline (same branch, env var unset).
- Metric: **TTFT** (time to first token) and **TPOT** (time per output token).
- Workload: cold cache for each (input tokens + output tokens) pair.
- Each run: 5 repetitions, report the **median**; standard deviation in parentheses when ≥ 1%.
- No kernel warmup excluded; results reflect end-to-end served latency.

| input+output | concurrency | vanilla TTFT (ms) | flaggems TTFT (ms) | TTFT Δ | vanilla TPOT (ms) | flaggems TPOT (ms) | TPOT Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50K+500 | 1 | 3965 | 3971 | ~0% | 10 | 10 | ~0% |
| 50K+500 | 10 | 23827 | 23050 | 3.26% | 60 | 62 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 1 | 486 | 483 | 0.62% | 8 | 8 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 10 | 1439 | 1153 | 19.87% | 38 | 28 | 26.32% |
| 1K+500 | 1 | 98 | 98 | ~0% | 8 | 7 | 12.50% |
| 1K+500 | 10 | 185 | 189 | ~0% | 17 | 17 | ~0% |

**Reading:** gains concentrate in the high-concurrency long-prompt case (10K+500, concurrency=10): ~19.87% TTFT / ~26.32% TPOT. Low-concurrency and short-prompt cases are neutral. The benefit is workload-specific, not universal.

## Purpose

Fixes #55581.

`FlashInferMetadataBuilder.get_cudagraph_support()` judges a KV-cache group's CUDA-graph support by dividing a query-head count by the group's `num_kv_heads`. The count comes from `vllm_config.model_config` — the target model. When speculative decoding adds a draft-side KV group, `_check_and_update_cudagraph_mode` hands that same target config into the draft group's arithmetic, so whenever the two models' head ratios differ the check computes the wrong ratio and spec decode silently loses every CUDA graph (the draft still runs via XQA).

The runner now judges each group against the config that owns the group: draft-side groups (`is_eagle_group=True`) get `speculative_config.draft_model_config`, everything else keeps the target config.

Run in a Linux container (python:3.12-slim, CPU torch): the new test passes
(1 passed). The file's teardown hooks raise a pre-existing

error appears on existing tests in this file (e.g.

items.title: [Bugfix] Support GPTQ-quantized DFlash draft models in the context-KV precompute path
items.body:
# [Bugfix] Support GPTQ-quantized DFlash draft models in the context-KV precompute path

## Summary

Quantized (GPTQ) DFlash draft models fail to load with:

```
AttributeError: 'QKVParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'. Did you mean: 'qweight'?
```

`DFlashModel._build_context_kv_buffers` slices `qkv_proj.weight[q_size:]` to build the fused K/V weight buffer used by `precompute_and_store_context_kv`. GPTQ/Marlin linears only keep packed parameters (`qweight`/`qzeros`/`scales`), no float `.weight`, so any GPTQ-quantized DFlash draft (e.g. an INT4 quantization of `z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash`) aborts during weight loading.

## Fix

In `_build_context_kv_buffers`, route through a new helper that:

- for float projections (`UnquantizedLinearMethod`) keeps the existing `.weight[q_size:]` slice — the fused single-GEMM path is untouched;
- for GPTQ projections (`AutoGPTQLinearMethod`) dequantizes the packed weight and slices the K/V rows from the reconstructed float weight;
- raises `NotImplementedError` for any other quantized method (their parameters do not follow the GPTQ layout this path reads) instead of silently reading wrong attributes.

The dequantization reads the **checkpoint layout**, which is the parameter state while `load_weights` runs — `process_weights_after_loading` converts to the Marlin layout afterwards, and the fused buffers built here are standalone tensors, so no interaction with the Marlin conversion. Layout handled:

- `qweight`: `[in/8, out]` int32, 8 4-bit codes per word, LSB first, along the input axis (input column `i = 8w + b` holds code `b` of word `w`);
- `scales`: `[in/group_size, out]`;
- `qzeros`: `[in/group_size, out/8]` int32, 8 4-bit zero points per word, LSB first, along the output axis.

Reconstruction is `(code - zero) * scale` with unsigned zero points; symmetric quantizers simply store `8` in every zero-point nibble (verified against the original BF16 draft weights: RMS abs error 0.0075 — quantization-noise level — versus 0.17 for a wrong zero-point interpretation).

## Why this approach

The context-KV precompute deliberately fuses all layers' K/V projections into a single float GEMM for performance. Two alternatives were considered and rejected:

1. Running each layer's quantized `qkv_proj` forward instead of the fused GEMM — correct but loses the fusion, and would need to move buffer construction out of `load_weights` (the linear methods are not usable until `process_weights_after_loading` runs).
2. Exposing a dequantize API on the quant method — cleaner long-term, but a much larger API surface change; the model-local helper keeps the change scoped to the DFlash path.

## Validation (manual)

- Draft: INT4 GPTQ quantization of `z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash` (`group_size=128`, `desc_act=False`, `sym=True`); target: `Qwen3.5-9B` GPTQ (mssfj), vLLM 0.28.0, RTX 4090.
- Server loads, serves and generates coherent output; speculative acceptance 21.5% — identical to the unquantized BF16 draft — and the tool-calling cycle works end to end.
- Throughput (same script, 512 output tokens, 3 runs):
  - BF16 draft: 269–272 tok/s
  - INT4 draft (this fix): 304–307 tok/s
  - no speculation baseline: 128 tok/s
- Unquantized-draft behavior unchanged (same code path, `isinstance` guard only).

## Test plan

Unit test for the dequantization helper is included (CPU, synthetic weights, no model download). Model-level coverage would require a quantized DFlash draft checkpoint in HF Hub, which does not exist publicly today; happy to add one if maintainers point at the preferred test-model org.

items.title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add PARD-2 parallel draft model support with dual mode
items.body:
## Purpose

Add PARD-2 ([arXiv 2605.08632](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08632)) target-aligned parallel draft models as a speculative-decoding method, and fix a draft-input alignment bug that costs most of the acceptance on one of the three released checkpoints.

This builds directly on @ganeshr10's work in #49406 — the first seven commits here are his, unmodified. That PR has been open since July and its benchmarks were run on CPU; I'm one of the PARD-2 authors, and in validating it on GPU I found that the draft is fed a left-shifted sequence, which drops the row PARD-2 was trained to start from. The last two commits fix that and add regression tests. I'm opening this as a separate PR because the fix is not meaningful on its own (it only touches the code path #49406 introduces) and #49406 has had no maintainer review in six weeks; I'd be equally happy for this to land as #49406 plus my two commits, whichever maintainers prefer. Closes/supersedes #49406.

### What PARD-2 is, and why add it

PARD converts an autoregressive draft model into a parallel one at low training cost; PARD-2 adds target alignment, optimizing acceptance length rather than next-token accuracy, plus confidence-adaptive token weighting. Two properties are relevant for vLLM:

- **The draft is a small standalone LM, not a head grafted onto the target.** One draft serves a whole model family.
- **Dual mode.** The same checkpoint runs target-dependent (fusing target hidden states) or target-independent (plain parallel drafting). This PR already handles the fallback when the target's hidden size doesn't match what the draft was trained on.

Measured in vLLM on an RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (greedy, 256 max tokens, 80 prompts per dataset, concurrency 1, PARD-2's own eval prompts), acceptance length / output tok/s. Baseline without speculation is 74 tok/s for both 8B targets:

| target | method | K | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | **PARD-2** `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` | 15 | **7.72 / 398** | **8.09 / 417** | **8.72 / 443** | **4.02 / 214** |
| | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` | 15 | 5.87 / 315 | 7.07 / 374 | 7.77 / 406 | 3.29 / 180 |
| | **PARD-2** | 5 | 4.86 / 255 | 5.00 / 262 | 5.09 / 266 | 3.44 / 183 |
| | EAGLE-3 `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3` | 5 | 2.69 / 150 | 2.53 / 141 | 2.85 / 158 | 2.24 / 125 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | **PARD-2** `amd/PARD2-Llama-3.1-8B` | 15 | **6.83 / 345** | **7.66 / 388** | **8.88 / 439** | **4.25 / 220** |
| | **PARD-2** | 9 | 6.06 / 310 | 6.37 / 326 | 7.12 / 358 | 4.05 / 210 |
| | DFlash `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat` | 9 | 4.19 / 230 | 3.62 / 200 | 5.65 / 306 | 3.61 / 200 |
| | EAGLE-3 `yuhuili/EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B` | 5 | 3.64 / 197 | 3.13 / 171 | 4.16 / 224 | 3.34 / 181 |

EAGLE-3 here is vLLM's chain drafting (no tree) in non-thinking mode, and the AngelSlim Qwen3 draft may be tuned for thinking traces — read those rows as "what the released weights give you in vLLM today", not as the method's ceiling.

### The bug this fixes

PARD-2's draft input for position *t* is `embed(token[t]) + scale · target_proj(feat[t-1])` with `feat[-1] = 0`: the draft sees the whole sequence, starting at token 0 paired with a zero target feature.

The draft goes through the EAGLE input path, which left-shifts the token stream (`shift_input_ids=True`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py`) while mapping hidden states unshifted. Row *i* of the draft input then holds `token[i+1] + feat[i]` — the correct pairing for *t ≥ 1*, but the *t = 0* row is gone. That is right for EAGLE, whose draft starts at token 1, and wrong for PARD-2.

That first row acts as an attention sink for the draft. How much its absence costs is checkpoint-dependent (HF reference, K=1 first-position acceptance, with vs. without token 0): Qwen3-8B 0.933 → 0.512, Llama-3.1-8B 0.937 → 0.917, Qwen3-14B 0.939 → 0.923.

**The fix**: an `ANCHOR` mode in `copy_and_expand_eagle_inputs_kernel`, used for PARD-2 only. A request whose first target position is 0 (its prefill) gets one extra leading row — its first token, position 0, zero hidden state — and its real rows shift by one so they keep true positions. Any other request instead gets one trailing junk row marked rejected, keeping the per-request row count uniform, and its draft `seq_len` grows by one for the anchor entry already in the draft KV cache. The CPU backend swaps this kernel for a C++ op that doesn't know about the anchor, so `cpu_triton_utils` gains a torch implementation of the same layout.

## Test Plan

```bash
# unit: anchored layout, and Triton ANCHOR path vs the CPU backend's torch path
pytest -v -s tests/v1/spec_decode/test_pard2_anchor_kernel.py

# e2e acceptance length (Llama case pre-existing, Qwen3-8B case added here)
pytest -v -s tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/pard2/

# serving
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8010 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B", "num_speculative_tokens": 15}'
```

Acceptance length is read from the `vllm:spec_decode_*` metrics; clients were greedy with `enable_thinking=false`.

## Test Result

Acceptance length before → after the fix, K=15, all three released checkpoints:

| target / draft | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B / `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` | 1.99 → **7.72** | 2.23 → **8.09** | 2.06 → **8.72** | 1.59 → **4.02** |
| Qwen3-14B / `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-14B` | 7.42 → **7.63** | 7.99 → **8.12** | 8.51 → **8.71** | 3.95 → **4.02** |
| Llama-3.1-8B / `amd/PARD2-Llama-3.1-8B` | 6.08 → **6.83** | 6.77 → **7.66** | 7.79 → **8.88** | 3.82 → **4.25** |

All twelve improve; none regress.

Cross-checked against the PARD-2 reference implementation on the same prompts, and against the paper (Table 1, K=16, GSM8K):

| checkpoint | paper | reference impl | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 7.68 | 7.62 | 1.99 | **7.72** |
| Qwen3-14B | 7.65 | 7.61 | 7.42 | **7.63** |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 6.98 | 6.89 | 6.08 | **6.83** |

Across all twelve (model × dataset) settings the fixed path is within 0.25 of the reference implementation, except on the 20-problem MATH-500 subset (±0.5).

Mixed prefill/decode batches, Qwen3-8B GSM8K at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32: acceptance 7.72 / 7.70 / 7.52, throughput 398 / 2351 / 3231 tok/s.

### Target-independent mode

PARD-2's draft is a standalone small LM, so the same checkpoint can drive a target it was never trained for; this PR falls back to plain parallel drafting when the target's hidden size doesn't match what `target_proj` was trained on. To put a number on that, `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` is used **unchanged** as a draft for **Qwen3-4B**, alongside drafts trained specifically for Qwen3-4B.

DFlash2 is not in this branch's base, so those rows ran on a current upstream-main nightly (`0.28.1rc1.dev19`). The `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` row was run on both builds and they agree within 0.12 (0.45 on the 20-problem MATH-500 subset), so the two groups are comparable. Same harness and settings as above; `acceptance / tok/s`.

**K = 15**

| build | draft | trained for Qwen3-4B? | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | **6.10 / 473** | 6.66 / 516 | 6.37 / 494 | **3.32 / 269** |
| this PR | PARD-1 `amd/PARD-Qwen3-0.6B` (parallel) | no | 6.06 / 466 | 6.01 / 464 | 6.10 / 465 | 3.37 / 267 |
| this PR | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` | yes | 5.71 / 484 | **6.87 / 582** | **6.70 / 565** | 3.22 / 285 |
| main | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` (build calibration) | yes | 5.83 / 504 | 6.42 / 557 | 6.70 / 575 | 3.21 / 290 |
| this PR | no speculation | — | — / 127 | | | |

**K = 8 / 7**, each DFlash2 checkpoint at its own trained block size, with PARD-2 at the same K:

| build | draft | trained for Qwen3-4B? | K | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | 8 | 5.27 / 412 | **5.43 / 424** | **5.29 / 409** | **3.19 / 255** |
| main | DFlash2 `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dflash2` (b9) | yes | 8 | **5.36 / 455** | 5.29 / 460 | 4.73 / 412 | 3.08 / 275 |
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | 7 | **5.02 / 394** | **5.23 / 407** | **5.04 / 387** | **3.16 / 251** |
| main | DFlash2 `shanjiaz/dflash2_qwen3_4b` (b8) | yes | 7 | 4.68 / 402 | 4.47 / 390 | 4.42 / 382 | 2.91 / 259 |

A draft that was never trained for this target holds its own against drafts that were: even on GSM8K and MATH-500 with DFlash2 at K=8, ahead of it on HumanEval and MT-Bench, and ahead of the other DFlash2 checkpoint on all four at K=7. DFlash2 is ~10% faster per token, its draft being 5 layers. Note both DFlash2 checkpoints are community-trained with `speculators` (z-lab has not released a 4B DFlash2) and were converted to the `dflash_config` layout to load, so read them as "DFlash2 as trained by the community", not as the method's ceiling.

## Notes for reviewers

- The two anchor commits touch `utils.py`, `llm_base_proposer.py` and `cpu_triton_utils.py` only; the ANCHOR path is a `tl.constexpr` branch, so EAGLE/DFlash/DSpark codegen is unchanged.
- `AutoWeightsLoader` lost its `skip_prefixes`/`skip_substrs` kwargs in #53106, so the PARD-2 draft would not load on current main; the last commit ports that call site the same way #53106 migrated the others.
- The per-dataset tables were measured before rebasing onto current main. After the rebase I re-ran GSM8K on the submitted tree end to end and reproduced it: acceptance 1.976 -> 7.618, throughput 109 -> 398 tok/s (previously 1.986 -> 7.715, 110 -> 398). Unit tests, the Triton-vs-CPU kernel comparison, and lint all pass on the submitted tree.

items.title: [Model] Add Qwen3 KSA support
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for Qwen3 models using KSA (Key-Value
cache with Summary Attention), validated with
[`OpenOneRec/KSA-4B-base`](https://huggingface.co/OpenOneRec/KSA-4B-base).

KSA inserts compressed Summary states inside the model while keeping the
scheduler-visible sequence text-only. Summary token IDs are never exposed
through logits, sampling, streaming output, or request accounting.

The implementation includes:

- model-internal Summary row expansion;
- separate Text and compressed Summary KV cache ownership;
- sliding-window Text cache for small-window layers;
- full Text attention without persistent Summary cache for large-window layers;
- Triton paged-attention kernels for prefill and decode;
- chunked prefill, continuous batching, preemption, pipeline parallelism,
  prefix caching, and restricted CUDA Graph support;
- fail-closed validation for unsupported runtime configurations;
- model registry, documentation, unit tests, CUDA tests, and a real-checkpoint
  E2E test.

## Why a separate model implementation is required

The released checkpoint contains model-specific Summary Attention parameters
and inserts one internal Summary state after every eight text tokens.

Treating the checkpoint as ordinary `Qwen3ForCausalLM` would:

- omit the Summary rows;
- use the wrong attention visibility pattern;
- fail to load or use the Summary-specific parameters correctly;
- lose the intended KV-cache memory reduction.

The vLLM scheduler continues to own only normal text tokens. Summary rows are
created and removed inside the model implementation.

## KV-cache design

For small-window layers, KSA maintains:

- a 1,032-state sliding Text cache;
- one compressed Summary state per eight logical text tokens.

For large-window layers, KSA maintains:

- a full Text cache;
- no persistent Summary cache.

The hybrid KV-cache manager is required. Disabling it would promote the
sliding Text cache to a dense cache while retaining the Summary cache, which
could consume more memory than ordinary dense attention. The implementation
therefore rejects this configuration during model initialization.

For the public 36-layer KSA-4B configuration at 128K context, the
block-rounded active KV state count is approximately 34.97% of a dense cache:

| Cache layout | Approximate active BF16 KV |
| --- | ---: |
| Dense 36-layer cache | 18.00 GiB |
| KSA Text + Summary caches | 6.29 GiB |
| Reduction | 65.03% |

vLLM may enlarge the logical Summary block size while unifying physical page
sizes. This does not change the compression ratio: the number of blocks
decreases proportionally, and the total number of stored Summary states
remains `floor(sequence_length / 8)`.

## Model resolution

The current public checkpoint declares `Qwen3ForCausalLM` in `config.json`.
Until the model repository updates that field, the KSA architecture must be
selected explicitly:

```bash
vllm serve OpenOneRec/KSA-4B-base \
  --hf-overrides '{"architectures":["Qwen3KSAForCausalLM"]}' \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Prefix caching is supported in eager mode with `block_size=8`:

```bash
vllm serve OpenOneRec/KSA-4B-base \
  --hf-overrides '{"architectures":["Qwen3KSAForCausalLM"]}' \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --block-size 8
```

The model revision used by the E2E and initialization tests is pinned to:

```text
6b60859be46422fc5949a0e69d2a338c4a618c90
```

## Supported configurations

| Feature | Supported configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Device | NVIDIA CUDA |
| Model dtype | BF16 |
| KV-cache dtype | BF16 or `auto` resolving to BF16 |
| Eager inference | TP=1/2/4, PP=1/2 |
| Chunked prefill | Supported |
| Prefix caching | Eager, `block_size=8`, TP=1, PP=1 |
| CUDA Graph | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, compilation mode `NONE`, TP=1, PP=1 |
| Pipeline parallelism | Eager mode |
| Speculative decoding | Unsupported |
| Weight/KV quantization | Unsupported |
| DCP/PCP | Unsupported |
| Prompt embeddings | Unsupported |


## Correctness validation

The real-checkpoint E2E test uses a 1,033-token prompt, crossing the first
1,032-token sliding-window boundary.

Input token IDs:

```text
[100, 101, ..., 1132]
```

Three-token greedy continuation:

| Implementation | Token IDs |
| --- | --- |
| Hugging Face reference (`use_cache=False`) | `[82, 13, 220]` |
| vLLM paged KSA | `[82, 13, 220]` |

At the first window transition:

- top-10 token overlap: `10/10`;
- mean absolute logit error: `0.021031`;
- greedy token: exact match.

The expected E2E tokens come from the pinned Hugging Face remote implementation
and are independent of the vLLM cache implementation.

## Tests

All commands were run using the repository's uv environment.

### Pre-commit

```bash
uv run --no-sync pre-commit run \
  --from-ref upstream/main \
  --to-ref HEAD
```

Result: all hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX,
forbidden-import, and Markdown checks.

### Cache mapping and metadata

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/attention \
  -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_ksa_cache_mapping.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_ksa_metadata.py
```

Result: `8 passed`.

### Model unit tests

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/models/language/generation \
  -q tests/models/language/generation/test_qwen3_ksa.py
```

Result: `42 passed`.

### CUDA paged-attention tests

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/attention \
  -q tests/v1/attention/test_ksa_paged_attention.py
```

Result: `4 passed`.

### Registry import

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/models \
  -q tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports \
  -k Qwen3KSAForCausalLM
```

Result: `1 passed, 376 deselected`.

### Required dummy initialization

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest \
  -q tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset \
  -k Qwen3KSAForCausalLM
```

Result: `1 passed, 367 deselected`.

### Real-checkpoint E2E

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest \
  -q tests/models/language/generation/test_qwen3_ksa_e2e.py
```

Result: `1 passed`.

## Model evaluation

The public KSA-4B checkpoint was evaluated through the vLLM inference path on
the paper benchmarks available in the local evaluation suite, excluding

| RULER 8K | 90.42 |
| RULER 16K | 88.95 |
| RULER 32K | 86.67 |
| RULER 64K | 76.63 |
| RULER 128K | 73.10 |

## Commit structure

The PR is intentionally split into four reviewable commits:

1. KSA cache mapping and attention metadata;
2. CUDA paged-attention kernel;
3. Qwen3 KSA model implementation;
4. registry, documentation, and real-checkpoint E2E coverage.

Internal experiment scripts, progress documents, and one-off benchmark

items.title: Revert "[Nixl][PD] DCP support for MLA models" (#50611)
items.body:
## Suggested narrower fix (preferred over this revert)

The regression is one gated assignment. In `SparseAttnIndexer.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size`, the memoization is conditional:

```python
if isinstance(get_forward_context().attn_metadata, dict):
    self._cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = value
return value
```

When `attn_metadata` is not a `dict`, the value is **never** cached, so every subsequent forward re-enters `get_current_vllm_config()`. Outside a `set_current_vllm_config()` context that raises. Caching unconditionally on first access — or resolving the value eagerly in `Worker.initialize_from_config`, as the docstring says already happens — should fix this without a revert. **If a maintainer lands that, please close this PR.**

## Root cause

#50611 replaced an eager `__init__`-time read:

```python
self.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
```

with a lazy `@property` that resolves `get_current_vllm_config()` at **model forward time**. DeepSeek-V4-Flash forwards then fail:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 849, in forward_cuda
    self.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size,
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 791, in cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
    get_current_vllm_config().parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
AssertionError: Current vLLM config is not set.
```

EngineCore then fails to start and the server exits.

## Evidence

Build <https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/86170> (`Full CI run - daily`, commit 6cddad4). 3 newly-failing jobs, plus a 4th whose failure signature changed to this one:

## Summary

Add **AtomGit** as a third model download source, alongside HuggingFace and ModelScope, mirroring the `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` UX:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT=True
vllm serve hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B ...
```

- When `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT=True`, redirects `HF_ENDPOINT` to `https://hub.atomgit.com` early at import time (`vllm/env_override.py`), matching what the `atomgit_hub` SDK does on import; vLLM's existing HuggingFace download paths (config / tokenizer / weights / processors) work unchanged.
- Repo ids with 3+ path segments (e.g. `hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`) are normalized to the 2-segment form (`hf_mirrors-Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`) in `ModelConfig`, consistent with the atomgit SDK's `_normalize_repo_id`; 2-segment ids (e.g. `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`) are kept as-is.
- Reuses the token saved by `atomgit login` (`~/.atomgit/config.json`) as `HF_TOKEN`, exported only when the endpoint actually points at AtomGit so the credential is never sent to a third-party endpoint; robust against malformed config (non-dict JSON / non-string token) so `import vllm` never crashes.
- Normalization skips URLs, object-storage URIs (`s3://`, `gs://`, `az://`, `runai://`, ...) and absolute/relative paths, so existing features such as RunAI object storage are unaffected; when both `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` and `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT` are set, AtomGit takes precedence.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open PRs of vllm-project/vllm via the GitHub search API for `AtomGit`, `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT`, `atomgit download` and `atomgit in:title` — all returned 0 results. No duplicate PR exists.

- New unit test `tests/transformers_utils/test_utils.py::test_normalize_atomgit_repo_id`: covers 1/2/3/4-segment ids and exclusion of URLs / object-storage URIs / absolute paths

## Purpose

This PR adds D-Spark speculative decoding support for
[Ling 3.0 Flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash)
using the official
[Ling D-Spark checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-dspark).

Key changes:

- Register `LingDSparkModel` and reuse the existing Qwen3 D-Spark runtime.
- Validate and normalize the Ling target/draft checkpoint contract.
- Expose the BailingMoeV3 auxiliary hidden states required by D-Spark.
- Use the checkpoint's D-Spark `block_size` as the default number of draft
  tokens while respecting an explicitly configured `num_speculative_tokens`.
- Give the Ling dense draft an independent 128-token KV-cache block instead of
  inheriting the target's KDA-expanded global block size.

Ling uses an MLA/KDA target with a dense MHA draft. KDA increases the target's
global attention block size, but applying the same token block size to the
dense draft produces a much larger MHA page and substantially reduces the
shared KV-cache capacity.

The Ling draft therefore uses a local 128-token KV-cache block. This override
is specific to normalized Ling D-Spark checkpoints; other Qwen3 DFlash and
D-Spark models continue to use the global cache block size.

The value 128 follows the model geometry. Per TP rank, with `H = 32 / TP`, the
draft MHA page is `128 × H × 128 × 2 (K/V) × 2 bytes`, equal to the KDA FP32
recurrent matrix `H × 128 × 128 × 4 bytes`. The complete KDA page is larger
because it also contains convolution state. Since regular MHA supports physical
page padding, the draft page can be padded to the aligned MLA/KDA target page
while retaining its logical 128-token block.

Example launch:

```bash
vllm serve \
  inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash \
  --served-model-name Ling-3.0-flash-dspark \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --reasoning-parser ling3 \
  --compilation-config \
    '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":2048}' \
  --speculative-config \
    '{"method":"dspark","model":"inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}'

| Configuration | Correct | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Target-only reference | 1278 / 1319 | 96.8916% |

## Purpose

# Hy4 preview Usage Guide

  Hy4 preview is Tencent Hy's new-generation open-source Mixture-of-Experts language
  model. Its backbone has 770B total parameters with 49B activated per token across
  78 layers. The first layer uses a dense FFN; the other 77 layers use 256 routed
  experts (top-8) and 1 shared expert. A native MTP layer adds 10B total parameters
  (0.7B activated) for speculative decoding.

  On the architecture side, inspired by DeepSeek and GLM, the attention module employs Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention (Gated DSA) with IndexCache for cross-layer sparse index reuse. The residual pathway uses iHC (identity Hyper-Connections) to expand inter-layer information flow.

  ## vLLM Setup

  Choose one of the following setup methods.

  ### Using Docker

  ```bash
  docker run --gpus all \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    --ipc=host \
    -e VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1 \
    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
    vllm/vllm-openai:hy4-preview tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
      --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
      --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
      --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
      --enable-auto-tool-choice \
      --port 8000 \
      --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  Build vLLM from source:

  ```bash
  uv venv --python 3.12 --seed --managed-python
  source .venv/bin/activate
  git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
  cd vllm
  uv pip install --editable . --torch-backend=auto
  ```

  ## vLLM Deployment

  Start the FP8 model with MTP enabled:

  ```bash
  export VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1

  vllm serve tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
    --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  ## OpenAI Client Example

  Tencent recommends `temperature=0.9` and `top_p=1.0`. Reasoning defaults to
